title: Secondary Mathematics & Physical Sciences — Unified Assessment
subject: Secondary Mathematics & Physical Sciences
institution: St. Jude Collegiate Academy & Examinations Syndicate
instructions: Read each question carefully before attempting your answer.
Answer all questions in Section A, Section B, and Section C.
For Multiple Choice Questions, mark the single correct option clearly.
Write all steps and working clearly in the spaces provided; credit is awarded for clear mathematical method.
Electronic calculators with scientific notation capability are permitted.
Take g = 9.8 m/s² unless stated otherwise in the question.

questions.text: What are the roots of the quadratic equation $x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0$?
Which inequality represents the solution set for $3(x - 2) < 2x + 5$?
A ladder $13\text{ m}$ long leans against a vertical wall with its foot $5\text{ m}$ away from the base of the wall. What height does the ladder reach on the wall?
questions.markingGuide: Pythagorean theorem: h = sqrt{} = sqrt{} = sqrt{} = 12 m.

questions.text: A diver descends to a depth of $25\text{ m}$ in seawater of density $1025\text{ kg/m}^3$. Taking $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, what hydrostatic gauge pressure is exerted on the diver?
What is the exact numerical value of $\cos(60^\circ) + \sin(30^\circ) - \tan(45^\circ)$?
A solid metal cone of base radius $6\text{ cm}$ and height $12\text{ cm}$ is melted down and recast into identical small spheres each of radius $3\text{ cm}$. How many complete spheres are formed?
If $\cos \alpha = \frac{1}{3}$, what is the value of $\cos(2\alpha)$?
Calculate the kinetic energy of an athlete of mass $65\text{ kg}$ sprinting at a constant velocity of $8.0\text{ m/s}$.
Given matrices $A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 \end{pmatrix}$, compute the determinant $\det(2A - B)$.

Calculate the mass of calcium oxide ($\text{CaO}$) produced by the thermal decomposition of $25.0\text{ g}$ of pure calcium carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$). (Molar masses: $\text{Ca} = 40.08, \text{C} = 12.01, \text{O} = 16.00\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.markingGuide: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. M(CaCO3) = 100.09 g/mol. M(CaO) = 56.08 g/mol. Moles CaCO3 = 25.0 / 100.09 = 0.2498 mol. Mass CaO = 0.2498 * 56.08 = 14.01 g.

questions.text: In the reaction $2\text{FeCl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{FeCl}_3$, identify the species being oxidized and the species being reduced. State the change in oxidation states supporting your assignment.
questions.markingGuide: Fe2+ in FeCl2 increases oxidation state from +2 to +3 in FeCl3 (oxidation / electron loss). Elemental Cl2 decreases oxidation state from 0 to -1 in FeCl3 (reduction / electron gain).

questions.text: In $\triangle ABC$, a line segment $DE$ is drawn parallel to base $BC$ with $D$ lying on $AB$ and $E$ on $AC$. If $AD = 3\text{ cm}$, $DB = 5\text{ cm}$, and the area of $\triangle ADE = 18\text{ cm}^2$, calculate the area of quadrilateral $DBCE$.
questions.markingGuide: Ratio of sides AD/AB = 3 / (3+5) = 3/8. Ratio of areas = (3/8)^2 = 9/64. Area(ABC) = 18 * (64/9) = 128 cm^2. Area(DBCE) = 128 - 18 = 110 cm^2.

questions.text: A railway truck of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ travelling at $4.0\text{ m/s}$ collides and couples with a stationary truck of mass $800\text{ kg}$. Calculate the common velocity of the coupled trucks immediately following impact.
questions.markingGuide: Total momentum before = total momentum after. (1200)(4.0) + (800)(0) = (1200 + 800)v  implies  4800 = 2000v  implies  v = 2.4 m/s.

questions.text: Points $A, B, C, D$ lie consecutively on a circle such that $AB$ is parallel to $CD$. Prove that the diagonal line segments $AC$ and $BD$ are equal in length.
questions.markingGuide: Since AB || CD, alternate interior angles angle BAC = angle ACD. Angles in the same segment give angle BDC = angle BAC = angle ACD. Thus triangle PCD where P is diagonal intersection is isosceles. Combined with opposite angles of cyclic quad summing to 180, chord AC = BD.

subparts.label: (a)
subparts.text: Verify that $(x - 1)$ is a factor of $f(x)$ using the factor theorem.

questions.markingGuide: (a) f(1) = 1 - 6 + 11 - 6 = 0. (b) Synthetic division gives (x-1)(x^2-5x+6) = (x-1)(x-2)(x-3). (c) Sign chart shows solution [1, 2] U [3, infinity).

questions.text: The function $f(\theta) = 3\sin \theta + 4\cos \theta$ represents an oscillating electrical potential.

subparts.label: (a)
subparts.text: Express $f(\theta)$ in the auxiliary form $R\sin(\theta + \alpha)$, where $R > 0$ and $0 < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}$.

subparts.label: (b)
subparts.text: State the maximum voltage potential and find the smallest positive angle $\theta$ at which this maximum occurs.

questions.markingGuide: (a) R = sqrt{} = 5. tan(alpha) = 4/3  implies  alpha = 0.927 rad (or 53.13 deg). f(theta) = 5sin(theta + 0.927). (b) Maximum = 5. Occurs when theta + 0.927 = pi/2 = 1.571  implies  theta = 0.644 rad (36.87 deg).
